images.caption: Figure 1:An evaluation example with VIEScore2. The model predicts perceptual quality (PQ), semantic consistency (SC), and a16×1616\times 16defect grid, where red and amber denote visual artifacts and semantic misalignments. A parameter-free parser converts the predictions into natural language.

Figure 2:Overview of VIEScore2: data preparation, SFT and GRPO training, and inference. GRPO combines Dice, score, and format rewards. The parameter-free parser converts predicted scores and defect grids into explanations. GT denotes ground truth.

Figure 3:Selected defect-localization examples across six benchmarks. Red cells denote predictions and green outlines denote ground-truth defect regions. Numbers report per-image grid IoU. Additional qualitative examples and failure cases are provided in AppendixF.
Figure 5:RichHF annotations and their16×1616\times 16grid targets. Red and blue denote artifact and misalignment; “!” marks high annotation coverage.

images.caption: Figure 8:Localization before and after GRPO. Orange cells mark defects; values are per-image grid IoU. VIEScore2 (−GRPO-\mathrm{GRPO}) uses the SFT checkpoint; epochs 4 and 5 give identical predictions. VIEScore2 denotes the final model after GRPO.
Figure 9:A RichHF example with annotations, predictions, raw output, and the parameter-free parser’s explanation.
